title: Marginal 90% normal-error axes permit ellipse coverage from 51% to 90% at zero covariance
abstract: We tested whether two marginal 90% error quantiles specify a 90% probability ellipse. The NHC 2026 experimental cone description motivates this question. For exact normal component distributions, sharp sum-distribution bounds give ellipse coverage from 51.04% to 90.00%, even when signed covariance is zero. Independent normal components give 74.15%. Finite assignment problems reproduce the bounds with symmetric margins and zero covariance. A continuous non-normal example gives zero coverage. We give explicit normal-model scale factors and a paired-score calibration specification. The result is an audit of the literal marginal-quantile rule, not measured NHC product coverage. The public description can omit joint scaling or other steps. Actual paired errors and issued axes are needed to test the implementation.

display.caption: Analytic coverage bounds for one ellipse with axes equal to marginal 90% absolute-error quantiles. These are model results, not observed NHC coverage.
